loincs.longName: Aspartate aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma

refDefault.note: Mayo Clinic Laboratories adult-male interval (males ≥14 y: 8-48 U/L; females ≥14 y: 8-43 U/L). Note: AASLD/ACG cite a lower 'healthy/true-normal' upper limit of ~29-33 U/L for men for detecting NAFLD/chronic liver disease; conventional lab ULNs (e.g. the printed <40) run higher.

references.document: Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST) (GOT), Serum (test AST / unit code 8360) - Reference Values
references.quote: Males ≥14 years: 8-48 U/L; Females ≥14 years: 8-43 U/L. Reference values have not been established for patients <12 months of age.

why: Hepatocellular injury marker; released from damaged liver cells (also cardiac/skeletal muscle). Interpreted with ALT (AST:ALT ratio) to distinguish alcoholic vs other liver disease.

loincs.longName: Alanine aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma

refDefault.note: Mayo Clinic Laboratories interval (males ≥6 y: 7-55 U/L; females ≥6 y: 7-45 U/L). Note: AASLD/ACG recommend a lower 'healthy' upper limit of normal of ~29-33 U/L for men when screening for chronic liver disease; the conventional printed lab ULN (<41) is higher.

references.document: Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT) (GPT), Serum (test ALT / unit code 8362) - Reference Values
references.quote: Males ≥6 years: 7-55 U/L; Females ≥6 years: 7-45 U/L. Reference values have not been established for patients <12 months of age.

why: Most liver-specific aminotransferase; sensitive marker of hepatocellular injury (viral/steatotic/drug-induced hepatitis). Elevations often precede clinical signs.

loincs.longName: Gamma glutamyl transferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma

refDefault.note: Mayo Clinic Laboratories interval (males ≥16 y: 8-61 U/L; females ≥16 y: 5-36 U/L). Matches the patient's printed lab range. GGT rises in cholestasis/biliary obstruction and confirms hepatic (vs bony) origin of a raised ALP; also induced by alcohol and enzyme-inducing drugs.

references.quote: Males ≥16 years: 8-61 U/L; Females ≥16 years: 5-36 U/L.

why: Sensitive marker of hepatobiliary disease and cholestasis; used to confirm the hepatic source of an elevated ALP and as a marker of alcohol use / enzyme induction.

loincs.longName: Alkaline phosphatase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma

refDefault.note: Mayo Clinic Laboratories adult interval (≥19 years: 40-129 U/L); Mayo does not sex-partition the adult range. ALP rises in cholestasis and in bone disease; correlate with GGT to localize the source.

references.document: Alkaline Phosphatase, Serum (test ALP) - Reference Values
references.quote: ≥19 years: 40-129 U/L. Reference values apply to adults.

why: Marker of cholestasis/biliary obstruction (and bone turnover). Disproportionate ALP elevation suggests infiltrative or obstructive hepatobiliary disease; paired with GGT to separate hepatic from bony origin.

molarMassRef: PubChem CID 5280352 (Bilirubin), C33H36N4O6, molecular weight 584.7 g/mol (584.66214). Molar (SI) form reported in µmol/L; conversion mg/dL × 17.1 = µmol/L. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/Bilirubin

refDefault.note: Mayo Clinic Laboratories adult interval (≥18 years: 0.0-1.2 mg/dL). Equivalent SI ≈ 0-20.5 µmol/L (×17.1). Mildly raised unconjugated total bilirubin with normal enzymes is commonly Gilbert syndrome.

references.document: Bilirubin, Total, Serum (test BILIT / unit code 81785) - Reference Values
references.quote: ≥18 years: 0.0-1.2 mg/dL. Reference values have not been established for patients <12 months of age.

why: Total heme-catabolism pigment; elevation causes jaundice. Fractionation (direct vs indirect) plus enzyme pattern distinguishes hemolytic/Gilbert (unconjugated) from hepatocellular/cholestatic (conjugated) causes.

molarMassRef: PubChem CID 5280352 (Bilirubin), C33H36N4O6, molecular weight 584.7 g/mol (584.66214). Direct = conjugated bilirubin (same core molecule). Molar (SI) form in µmol/L; mg/dL × 17.1 = µmol/L. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/Bilirubin

refDefault.note: Mayo Clinic Laboratories interval (≥12 months: 0.0-0.3 mg/dL). Equivalent SI ≈ 0-5 µmol/L (×17.1). Conjugated (direct) bilirubin >0.3 mg/dL or a raised direct fraction indicates hepatobiliary/cholestatic disease.

references.document: Bilirubin, Direct, Serum (test BILID / unit code 81787) - Reference Values
references.quote: ≥12 months: 0.0-0.3 mg/dL. Reference values have not been established for patients <12 months of age.

why: Conjugated bilirubin fraction; elevation points to hepatocellular dysfunction or biliary obstruction (cholestasis) rather than hemolysis/Gilbert syndrome.

refDefault.note: Mayo Clinic Laboratories interval (≥1 year: 6.3-7.9 g/dL). Sum of albumin + globulins; interpret with albumin and the A/G ratio. Note the patient's printed lab range (6.20-8.50) is wider than Mayo's.

references.document: Protein, Total, Serum (test TP) - Reference Values
references.quote: ≥1 year: 6.3-7.9 g/dL. Reference values have not been established for patients <12 months of age.

why: Total of albumin plus globulins; screens for synthetic liver capacity, nutrition, and dysproteinemias. Low total protein with low albumin suggests impaired hepatic synthesis or loss; high globulin fraction raises paraproteinemia/chronic inflammation.

refDefault.note: Mayo Clinic Laboratories interval (≥12 months: 3.5-5.0 g/dL). Note the patient's printed lab range (3.50-5.40) has a higher ceiling than Mayo's. Low albumin marks reduced hepatic synthesis (chronic liver disease), loss (nephrotic/enteropathy), or inflammation.

references.quote: ≥12 months: 3.5-5.0 g/dL. Reference values have not been established for patients <12 months of age.

why: Major hepatic synthetic protein and oncotic driver; a marker of chronic liver synthetic function and nutritional/inflammatory status. Falls in cirrhosis, protein loss, and systemic inflammation (negative acute-phase reactant).

loincs.longName: Amylase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma

refDefault.note: Mayo Clinic Laboratories adult interval (≥18 years: 28-100 U/L; per 2022 Mayo/MLabs test update). Amylase is a pancreatic/salivary enzyme, not hepatic; not sex-partitioned. Value obtained via search-indexed Mayo catalog content — see reference URL.

references.document: Amylase, Total, Serum (test AMS / unit code 8352) - Reference Values
references.quote: Adults ≥18 years: 28-100 U/L (Mayo Clinic Laboratories / MLabs test update, 2022).

why: Pancreatic/salivary hydrolase; elevated in acute pancreatitis and pancreatic/salivary duct disease. Included with liver-panel enzymes to cover pancreatobiliary causes of abdominal pain (lipase is more specific).
